title: Sebastian and the Garden
premise: Cyrus Amberdale has hidden his beast-speaker gift for twenty years in Greyhollow, a city where magic is outlawed and informants are paid in bread. When the old gods suddenly begin answering prayers again, the animals start begging him for help — and the Ministry of Order begins hunting anyone who can hear them. Guided by a dying fox-god and a disgraced priestess named Wren, Cyrus discovers he is the last living signatory of the covenant that once bound gods, beasts, and humans together. To end the long winter falling over both realms, he must travel to the Garden where the covenant was first sworn and reforge it — at the cost of surrendering his memories of everyone he loves. In the end Cyrus pays the price, but Wren carries his story back to him, and in remembering aloud she gives him a new self built from truth rather than secrecy.
about_author: Juniper Villalobos grew up between her grandmother's orchard in Oaxaca and a drafty flat in Edinburgh, a childhood split between two languages and two kinds of weather. She writes quiet fantasies about people who talk to things that cannot answer back.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. On a frozen market morning, Cyrus sells a luck-knot to a grieving widow while his gift stays carefully silent — until a stray dog speaks to him for the first time in years, begging him to listen to the river. The beat: loneliness cracked open by an impossible voice.

chapters.title: What the River Said
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The river tells Cyrus the old gods are waking, and that something is wrong on the far side of the water. He reports nothing, but a Ministry clerk named Halvers notices him lingering at the bank. The beat: dread — the first thread of surveillance tightening around him.

chapters.title: A Fox at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. A red fox, half-starved and speaking with the cadence of a god, collapses in Cyrus's cellar. It names itself Vessel-of-Embers and asks for sanctuary. The beat: reluctant compassion; Cyrus breaks twenty years of caution in one night.

chapters.title: The Ministry of Order
chapters.summary: POV Halvers. The clerk investigates a spike in answered prayers across Greyhollow and is ordered to find 'listeners.' We see the regime's fear through its functionary's tired eyes. The beat: institutional menace, and Halvers' first flicker of doubt about his masters.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. A woman arrives at his shop asking for a charm against forgetting; her brand marks her as an ex-priestess of the old rites. She recognizes what Cyrus is before he admits it. The beat: wary alliance — two people deciding whether to trust each other.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered, Badly
chapters.summary: POV ensemble vignettes. Across the city, prayers come true in twisted ways: rain that won't stop, a dead child briefly returned. The waking gods are powerful but broken. The beat: wonder curdling into horror; stakes made city-wide.

chapters.title: The Covenant Broken
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren explains the old three-way covenant among gods, beasts, and humans, and how the Ministry's founders shattered it, exiling the gods into a starving half-realm. Cyrus learns his bloodline signed it. The beat: revelation reframing his small life as historically enormous.

chapters.title: Hunted
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Halvers raids the charm shop; Vessel-of-Embers escapes through the sewers but Cyrus is taken for questioning. He lies well enough to walk free — and hates how easily the skill comes. The beat: guilt and adrenaline; loyalty to the fox tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Frost spreads unnaturally from the river outward; crops fail in a week. The Ministry blames saboteurs and doubles the informant bounty. The beat: escalating catastrophe compressing every character's timeline.

chapters.title: Beasts at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Animals gather outside Greyhollow's walls, drawn to Cyrus like iron to a lodestone, asking their speaker to lead them somewhere they only know as the Garden. The beat: awe and burden — he can no longer pretend to be ordinary.

chapters.title: Halvers' Choice
chapters.summary: POV Halvers. Ordered to arrest the charm seller, Halvers instead reads confiscated records and learns the Ministry manufactured the original covenant-breaking. He burns one page and keeps one. The beat: a minor antagonist turning; conscience outweighing career.

chapters.title: Leaving Greyhollow
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus and Wren alternating. The trio slips out during a blizzard, pursued by Ministry riders. Wren confesses she once helped seal the gods away, believing it mercy. The beat: trust forged in flight; secrets traded as currency.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Sheltering in a flooded chapel, the group meets a river-god too weakened to speak, communicating through fish and reflections. It shows them the road to the Garden — and warns that the gate takes a toll. The beat: solemnity; the journey acquires a known price.

chapters.title: Country of Thorns
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Crossing the blighted borderlands, Cyrus hears thousands of beast-souls fraying as winter deepens. Vessel-of-Embers grows weaker with each mile, spending itself to keep the path open. The beat: grief in advance; love for a dying guide.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: POV Halvers. A fellow clerk betrays the party's route; Halvers must choose to warn them or cover himself. He sends the warning and flees the Ministry, becoming a fugitive mid-book. The beat: point of no return for the secondary arc.

chapters.title: The Garden Found
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Beyond the thorns lies the Garden: impossibly green at its heart, ringed in ice, full of sleeping gods and the ghost-echoes of the original signatories. Cyrus finds his ancestor's name carved beside empty space — space shaped exactly like him. The beat: destiny arriving as terror rather than glory.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The garden's warden-god states the terms: the covenant can be reforged only by a living signatory who surrenders all memory of those bound to him by love. Wren argues, rages, and finally stops arguing when Cyrus quietly agrees. The beat: heartbreak; the theme of memory made literal.

chapters.title: Night Before the Forgetting
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. One last evening: Cyrus asks Wren to tell him stories of his own life so some trace might survive inside hers. They speak until dawn — his mother, the shop, the fox asleep against his boots. The beat: tender, elegiac calm before sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus dissolving into third-person distance as his memories leave him. Blood on stone, names spoken, the covenant remade; the long winter cracks and retreats. Vessel-of-Embers dies content, becoming warmth in the new spring. The beat: climax — triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Spring, Without Him
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The world thaws; gods and beasts keep their side of the bargain. Cyrus wakes in the Garden gentle and blank, knowing no one. Wren brings him home to Greyhollow anyway. The beat: bittersweet aftermath; devotion without recognition.

chapters.title: Telling Him His Own Story
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Through a long summer, Wren tells Cyrus everything — and Halvers, now keeper of the burned page, corroborates the parts she wasn't there for. Cyrus begins choosing which truths to make his own. The beat: identity rebuilt as an act of communal storytelling.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Garden
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. He takes a new name — Sebastian — not as erasure but as authorship, and reopens the charm shop with a fox kit asleep in the cellar. When the river speaks again, he answers gladly. Final beat: wholeness; a self chosen, remembered, and freely given.
